title: No, the Organic Label is Not a Marketing Scam - Rodale Institute
summary: Rodale Institute defends the USDA organic seal as a rigorous, annually audited standard while noting loopholes on hydroponics, poultry porches and import fraud.

assertions.quote: Maybe you’ve heard that the organic label is just a marketing ploy, but that’s far from the truth.
can produce yields equal to conventional—if not higher
organic systems are more resilient, sequester more carbon, yield fewer emissions, require less energy
must undergo a yearly review and audit by a third-party certifier
the chickens’ “outdoor access” was to an enclosed porch rather than true pasture

verdicts.note: Porches have counted as outdoor access, but a 2023 USDA rule requires soil and vegetation outdoors, phased in by 2029 for existing farms.

assertions.quote: It is possible to buy a product with the organic label that was grown indoors under artificial light and without soil.
As organic has become more profitable, there’s been an increase in import fraud.
some shipments (usually livestock feed) claimed as organic were actually conventional
The farms must then implement additional practices to improve soil health, animal welfare, and social justice.
